speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what might be wrong, tell me: do you have trouble swallowing milk or solids, or does the food seem to get stuck in your throat?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Please describe the color of your baby's stools and whether there have been any episodes of forceful vomiting, especially if it looks like coffee grounds. Also, has your baby passed gas or had any bowel movements recently?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your baby ever passed meconium within the first 48 hours of life? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray to visualize the transition zone.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Jejunal Atresia.

The radiographic finding of dilated proximal bowel with a sharp transition zone and absent distal gas, combined with the lack of meconium passage, strongly indicates a jejunal obstruction. The absence of forceful bilious vomiting and fever helps rule out necrotizing enterocolitis or intestinal volvulus. Based on this clinical picture, the underlying condition is a congenital jejunal atresia, likely requiring surgical intervention.
